title: fix(fields): the two readonly datetime widget faces converge on formatDateTime, one face per register (objectui#8209)
body:
Fixes #8209

Ruling: objectui#8209 comment `5696850133` (director seat, batch #142 item 2, maintainer 「同意」). Letter = **per register**, both sites through the one home `formatDateTime`. Session: `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`.

## What changed

Two readonly `datetime` faces in `@object-ui/fields` composed a bare `toLocaleDateString(locale)` + `toLocaleTimeString(locale)` pair joined by a space. Neither went through `formatDateTime`, the one home objectui#7443 declared for this convention, so both carried seconds that no `datetime` cell has ever shown.

| site | register | face now | call |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `DateTimeField.tsx` readonly branch | form / detail | verbose **default** | `formatDateTime(value, { locale })` |
| `GridField.tsx` `temporalText`, `datetime` branch | grid cell | **`'compact'`** | `formatDateTime(dt, { style: 'compact', locale })` |

With this, objectui#7443's "`datetime` has one home" holds for all six bare no-bag sites objectui#8194 enumerated.

## ⚠️ ONE DEVIATION FROM THE RULING, and it is in the call shape, not the face

The ruling's call shape for the sub-grid is `formatDateTime(value, { style: field.format ?? 'compact', locale })`, on the stated basis that the sub-grid cell can read `field.format` "the way `DateTimeCellRenderer` does — reuse, not a new declaration".

**Measured: there is nothing there to reuse.** `temporalText` is handed a column `type`, a value and a locale — no field. Its caller holds a `GridColumn`, and neither `GridColumn` nor the published `GridColumnDefinition` it mirrors declares a `format` key at all. `DateTimeCellRenderer` reads `DateTimeFieldMetadata.format`, which is a field-metadata key that does not reach this surface.

So the authored read the ruling wrote could only be spelled by **declaring** `format` on the grid-column shape — which the very same ruling forbids in the next bullet ("⛔ No new widget style vocabulary … reuse, not a new declaration"), and which is the declared `Clause-②: no` fork.

⇒ The style is a **literal** `'compact'`. The ruled FACE is delivered exactly; only the read that would have selected it is absent, because the vocabulary it would have read does not exist here. The ruling's recorded fallback (both sites on the default face) is **not** taken: it is reserved for "if the per-register split proves unimplementable at the sub-grid", and the split is implementable — it is the `field.format` READ that is not. Choosing the fallback would have discarded the ruled grid-cell face over a spelling detail.

## The five-locale render table, re-taken

⛔ Not copied from the card. Re-measured by rendering both components through `I18nProvider`, `TZ=UTC`, value `2026-07-04T07:00:00.000Z`, on this branch.

| locale | before, both sites | after, readonly widget | after, sub-grid cell |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| en | `7/4/2026 7:00:00 AM` | `Jul 4, 2026, 07:00 AM` | `7/4/2026 7:00 am` |
| de | `4.7.2026 07:00:00` | `4. Juli 2026, 07:00` | `4.7.2026 7:00 am` |
| zh | `2026/7/4 07:00:00` | `2026年7月4日 07:00` | `2026/7/4 上午7:00` |
| ja | `2026/7/4 7:00:00` | `2026年7月4日 07:00` | `2026/7/4 午前7:00` |
| ar | `4/7/2026 7:00:00 ص` | `4 يوليو 2026، 07:00 ص` | `4/7/2026 7:00 ص` |

The `ar` rows carry U+200F marks around the date separators; omitted so the table stays readable. The **before** column reproduces the card's measured table byte for byte on today's `main`.

**The year is not dropped.** Every "after" cell carries `2026`, in both registers. The year-drop is `formatDate`'s date-only cell rule under objectui#7620 and nothing here extends it.

## The flip pin comes first, and it is in two halves

A test that only asserts the new faces does not witness the change — it would pass identically in a tree where the second convention had never existed. So:

- **Negative half** — objectui#8194's `SCOPE FENCE` block, converted in place to `FENCE LIFTED`. The removed spelling stays copied **verbatim** (`toLocaleDateString` + `toLocaleTimeString`, no bag, space-joined) and both sites are now asserted to have LEFT it, five locales each. Plus a fixture-validity case pinning that the removed pair still carries the seconds neither new face shows.
- **Positive half** — new `datetime-widget-faces-8209.test.tsx`: each site equals its ruled face asked of the shared function, in five locales; each site is asserted NOT to render the other register's face; the `en` literals the ruling quotes; the no-year-drop claim in all five locales plus a past year; and the empty / unparseable faces.

The fixture is built as July 4, 07:00 in the **runner's** zone rather than from an ISO `07:00Z` literal, so the `en` literals are exact in every timezone.

### Four sibling pins asserted the former faces, and were updated deliberately

The face move turned four existing cases red. None is a repair of this branch's own breakage — each is a pin of the string that just moved:

- `datetime-widgets.test.tsx` — the readonly `DateTimeField` case, rewritten onto the verbose default bag, mirroring how objectui#8194 rewrote the `DateField` case sitting directly above it.
- `__tests__/date-locale-channel.test.tsx` — expressed through a new `defaultDateTimeFace()` helper, the idiom that file already uses for `date`. That file's subject is WHICH TAG reaches `Intl`, so it now asserts the `zh` face present and the `en` face absent instead of a bare literal.
- `widgets/GridField.test.tsx` — two cases, now asking the shared formatters for both expectations.

⚠️ **One of those four was passing for the wrong reason, and it is worth a look.** `expectedDay` in `GridField.test.tsx` was `Intl`'s bare numeric default, `6/17/2026` — a string the `datetime` cell beside it CONTAINS. Since objectui#8194 moved the `date` column to `Jun 17`, `toContain(expectedDay)` had been satisfied by the wrong column, and would have stayed green with the `date` column rendering anything at all. Both faces are now named, and a `FIXTURE VALIDITY` case pins that the three temporal faces are three distinct strings.

### Narrowing, declared

The rendered text that moved belongs to two components. No file outside `packages/fields/` names `DateTimeField`, `GridField`, `LineItemsField` or `line-items-readonly`; `toLocaleTimeString` occurs nowhere outside that package; and a search of every dependent package's tests for a seconds-bearing clock literal returns only a debug drawer's own fixture strings and two timestamps inside a prose comment — with a positive control in the same query shape firing inside `packages/fields`. So the full `@object-ui/fields` suite plus the repo-wide run CI owns is the coverage this change needs; ⛔ the dependents' suites were not run locally.

### Census re-derived, not trusted

The card's mechanism census was re-derived on today's `main` (`ff29450a9`) rather than taken from the card. `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `toDateString`, `toUTCString`, `date-fns`, `dayjs`, `luxon` — zero, with `toLocaleDateString` as the lit control in the same query shape. Every `moment` hit is the English word in prose. Two measured drifts from the card, neither load-bearing: the package now has **81** non-test source files, not 78, and `toLocaleString` (number formatting) occurs **3** times, not 4. Live-code `toLocale*` date sites before this change: exactly the **two** the card names — the other five `toLocaleDateString` hits are objectui#8194's own comments.

## Acceptance notes

- `pnpm check:changeset-claims` reports (report-only) that the pending `.changeset/6625-retire-fieldmeta-decimals.md` names `GridField.tsx`, which this branch edits. Read and answered: that paragraph is about `.decimals` / `.scale` member reads, this diff adds and removes none, and the `scale` occurrence count in `GridField.tsx` is unchanged at 3. The claim stands.
- The `—` a readonly `datetime` widget now shows for an unparseable value is `formatDateTime`'s own hand-rolled dash, so it carries no `empty-value` slot and no accessible name — unlike the absent-value branch beside it. That is the objectui#8490 / objectui#8581-class gap, it predates this card at every site objectui#8194 converged too, and widening it is a display decision nobody has ruled. Recorded as an assertion in the new pin so the difference is visible rather than assumed away; noted, not filed — the carrier that would pick it up is whatever revisits the shared empty affordance across the `date` family.
